base_override.reason: BASE_DIVERGENCE resolution: both candidate bases are distorted. The latest FY ($31.5901) is flattered by the ARKA acquisition year — deferred income taxes added $145,387,000 to FY2026 OCF (vs -$27,060,000 in FY2025, per the FY2026 earnings-release cash-flow statement) as the ARKA purchase-accounting deferred tax liability built, working-capital drag eased, and ARKA contributed only a ~4-month stub. The 3-yr median ($18.8107) is depressed the other way: FY2024–25 OCF margins of ~6.5% / ~6.3% were the low end of the decade range while receivables built through 14–15% revenue-growth years, and it assigns zero weight to the ARKA step-up that FY2027 guidance (free cash flow of at least $900M, earnings release) corroborates. The 3-yr mean splits the two distortions. Measured impact (engine --measure, identical other inputs): median base prints Tier D (weighted IRR 8.22%, IV@15% $259.93 at default growth), mean base at default growth prints Tier D (9.23%, $309.64), latest-FY base prints Tier C (11.71%, $436.52) — no base clears 15%, so the verdict does not rest on the override.

moat_against: ROIC proxy only 7.6–11.5% over the last decade (fundamentals.json) — no wide-moat economics; FY2026 ROIC fell to 7.6% on the ARKA capital base
Contracts recompete: incumbency is rented, not owned; Leidos, Booz Allen, GDIT, SAIC and Peraton bid the same task orders
Single-customer complex: US federal budgets, procurement delays, shutdowns and administration priorities set demand
People-based delivery limits pricing power; wage pressure on cleared staff flows straight to margin
Growth partly acquired, not organic: ARKA cost $2.6B cash and FY2026 revenue growth was 10.9% total vs 7.2% organic
moat_for: Classified incumbency and cleared workforce — high barriers to entry on intelligence / DoD mission programs
Differentiated owned technology (SIGINT, electronic warfare, space-based sensors via ARKA) vs pure labor-hour services
$32.0B total backlog (~3.3x FY2026 revenue), funded backlog +29% YoY, FY2026 book-to-bill 1.1x — multi-year revenue visibility
Mix shift to technology lifting profitability: operating margin 8.0% (FY2022) → 9.6% (FY2026), EBITDA margin 12.3%
~90% national-security concentration in enduring, well-funded budget priorities; federal civilian exposure largely exited
moat_justification: Classified incumbency, a cleared workforce and differentiated owned technology in SIGINT / electronic warfare / space sensors (ARKA) are real advantages, and the technology mix shift lifted operating margin from 8.0% (FY2022) to 9.6% (FY2026) — but the ROIC proxy in fundamentals.json has run only 7.6–11.5% over the last decade (FY2022–26: 8.6% / 9.4% / 10.2% / 9.4% / 7.6%), barely above the cost of capital, contracts are periodically recomped against Leidos / Booz Allen / GDIT / SAIC, the US government is effectively a single monopsonist customer, and growth is partly bought (ARKA, $2.6B cash, closed 2026-03-09). That is a moderate, narrow moat — not a wide one.
